messages:
ACME Support (customer): Hey team, we're seeing intermittent disconnects from the dedicated instance when streaming responses. Client sees partial output then reconnects and sometimes gets duplicated tokens. Happens only for our corp network behind the company proxy + VPN. Started yesterday after we bumped batch size. Example from a user session: `...\nPartial text: "The quick brown fox"` then connection closes; client reconnects and resumes at start of response. Also saw occasional 401 on reconnect even though token is valid. Any ideas?

Maya K.: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a raw curl that reproduces it and a short tcpdump or browser console output? Also which model and sequence length?

ACME Support (customer): Repro is simple: `curl -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \"https://dedicated.acme.redwood/api/v1/stream?model=rw-medium&seq=2048\"` From the browser console: `EventSource error` and the client saw a single SSE comment then nothing. We captured a tcpdump; I pasted a small excerpt below:

```
14:22:01.123456 IP client -> proxy: Flags [P.], seq 1:1461, ack 1, win 64240, length 1460
14:22:01.123789 IP client -> proxy: Flags [P.], seq 1461:2921, ack 1, length 1460
14:22:01.124000 IP client -> proxy: Flags [P.], seq 2921:4381, ack 1, length 1460
14:22:01.500000 IP proxy -> backend: Flags [P.], seq 1:137, ack 1, length 136
# note the MSS/MTU suggests fragmentation on path
```

ACME Support (customer): Also seeing occasional `502 Bad Gateway` from proxy logs around the same timestamps.

Liam S.: Sounds like MTU/fragmentation + proxy buffering. Corporate proxies often reassemble differently and may drop long-lived chunked transfers if they think the connection is idle or don't support indefinite streaming. Two simultaneous things to check: (1) MTU path (PMTUD) between client and our edge, and (2) proxy buffering/timeouts.

Eli R.: Quick checklist: 
- Check VPC route MTU and whether there's an AWS Transit Gateway or NAT gateway reducing effective MTU to < 1500 (we've seen 1400 on some corporate VPNs).
- Ask the customer to run `tracepath`/`ping -M do -s` to see fragmentation.
- On our side, confirm we send SSE comment keepalives (the runtime sends `: heartbeat\n\n` every 15s) — if the proxy strips comments or drops long streaming due to no "real" data the proxy may close.

Maya K.: Can you upload proxy logs showing why it returned 502? Also does the client get a TCP FIN or RST? If it's RST from proxy it's likely proxy buffer overflow/timeouts.

ACME Support (customer): Uploaded anonymized proxy logs to the ticket. Proxy shows `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream` and NGINX has `proxy_buffering off` actually set, but `proxy_busy_buffers_size` shows spikes. I also see `request timed out` entries with 60s default.

Liam S.: Two mitigations to try while we triage: 
1) Server side: enable more frequent SSE keepalives (every 5-10s) or send a tiny chunked JSON heartbeat object so proxies don't treat stream as idle. e.g. `:\n\n` or `data: {\"hb\":1}\n\n`
2) Client side: implement idempotent resume logic (server should include a streaming-uuid and last-token-index so clients can safely dedupe on reconnect). Also ensure client reuses same auth token — 401 on reconnect might be due to short-lived token refresh race.

Eli R.: For dedicated/private customers behind proxies we also recommend: 
- Increase `proxy_read_timeout` and `proxy_send_timeout` to 300s on NGiNX; `proxy_buffer_size` and `proxy_buffers` to handle larger chunks.
- If corporate proxy does TLS interception, ensure it supports chunked transfer and long-lived responses; some older proxies will convert chunked into buffered requests and then tear them down.

Maya K.: Can you try a quick repro with chunk sizes forced small from our runtime (we can flip a flag to emit smaller SSE chunks) and with keepalive set to 5s from the dedicated instance? That will prove whether it's an idle timeout vs. fragmentation issue.

ACME Support (customer): We tried server keepalive at 5s and the stream stayed open for ~10 minutes while returning tokens, much better. After ~30 minutes the proxy still cut the connection and then we got duplicate tokens on client resume. Also still saw the occasional 401 after reconnect.

Liam S.: Duplicate tokens likely from client replaying last N tokens on reconnect; make server side idempotency key (stream-id + token-index) so if a client resends it just skips duplicates. For the 401: can you confirm whether there is an auth middleware that validates ephemeral sessions per TCP connection? Some corporate proxies mutate headers and may strip `Authorization` on reconnect attempts.

ACME Support (customer): Proxy is adding `Via:` and a few headers, but not intentionally stripping Authorization. We'll confirm.

sre-bot: Deploy completed to dedicated pool-3: commit abc123. No config flips.

Eli R.: Next steps from our side: 
- We'll enable a toggle on the customer instance to (a) reduce chunk size, (b) aggressive keepalive 5s, (c) add `stream-id` header so reconnects are safer.
- Eng-runtime will add server-side duplicate token detection within the session window.
- Eng-platform to produce a troubleshooting note for customers: commands for `tracepath`, `ping` with `-M do`, and sample nginx settings: 
```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_read_timeout 300s;
proxy_send_timeout 300s;
proxy_buffer_size 16k;
proxy_buffers 8 32k;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```
Maya K.: I filed a medium-sev ticket and assigned to eng-runtime + eng-platform. Tagging @eli and @liam for follow-up.

ACME Support (customer): Thanks — after the toggle the sessions are much more stable. We'll keep the toggle for now and test from several office locations to verify. Also will check whether their VPN stack reduces MTU to 1400 which may be the root cause for fragmentation we saw.

Liam S.: If you need a quick client patch, we can push a small client SDK change that dedups tokens based on stream-id + index and retries auth exchange before resuming. Could avoid billing spikes from duplicate generation.

ACME Support (customer): Please do — that would help. Marking this thread as actionable. :thumbsup:

Maya K.: Closing loop once eng posts the change. Thanks everyone.
